systems.name: null
systems.title: the harness alone: a pointer handed over in one thread, nothing sent
systems.notes: Not a system: the floor. What its row shows is the cost of the two clock readings and, under "intended", the schedule's own lateness. One process, so no subscriber count above 1, no start-up, and its CPU is the publisher loop's.

systems.name: hangar
systems.title: hangar, lib/hg: a topic with a 16-slot ring in shared memory, the reader woken by one futex
systems.notes: The message is copied into the ring and out of it. A reader that falls 16 messages behind loses the oldest (counted as lost): the writer never waits.

systems.name: hangar-inplace
systems.title: hangar, lib/hg, in place: the publisher fills a loaned slot, the reader is handed a view of it
systems.notes: Nothing is copied. The view is checked after the harness has read it; one the writer overwrote meanwhile is dropped and counted (discarded, and then lost).

systems.name: unix-seqpacket
systems.title: Unix domain sockets, SOCK_SEQPACKET: the kernel's own IPC, no middleware
systems.max_size_why: a message must fit the socket's send buffer whole: 212992 B by default, and more needs privileges
systems.install: make pairs, or the baselines archive: --var base=<its bin directory>
systems.notes: The floor for anything that sends through the kernel. The reader sleeps in recv and is woken by the kernel: no polling. Two copies (user to kernel, kernel to user) and one system call a side. The publisher never waits: a subscriber whose buffer is full does not get the message, and a socket then drops the newest and keeps the old, where hangar's ring drops the oldest. The buffer's depth is the kernel's accounting of bytes (net.core.wmem_default), some hundreds of small messages, not 16. No helper, no discovery beyond a path, no type, no metadata.

systems.name: unix-stream
systems.title: Unix domain sockets, SOCK_STREAM: the same for any size, the writer waiting for the reader
systems.install: make pairs, or the baselines archive: --var base=<its bin directory>
systems.notes: What a megabyte through a socket is: a run of bytes, several send and receive calls a message, two copies. Another contract than the others': the publisher's send blocks while the reader's buffer is full, so nothing is ever lost and a slow reader slows the writer (it shows under "intended"). With several subscribers the publisher writes to each in turn. The reader has the message when it has collected all its bytes.
